title: perf: share the base PrimitiveComponent config instead of rebuilding per access (#2810)
description: Reduces memory allocation by sharing the base PrimitiveComponent configuration instead of creating a new instance on each access.
body:
Progress on #2810 — the low-risk first slice of the suggested pure-TS fix.

## Change

The base `PrimitiveComponent.get config()` constructed a **fresh** `z.object({}).passthrough()` on every access:

```ts
get config(): BaseComponentConfig {
  return { componentName: "", zodProps: z.object({}).passthrough() }
}
```

`config` is a plain getter with no memo cache, accessed thousands of times per build, and each Zod v3 schema instance eagerly binds ~15 methods (`.parse`, `.safeParse`, `.refine`, …). The heap snapshot in tscircuit/tscircuit#4077 shows ~714k `native_bind` closures retained across ~47k schema instances, with the non-memoized base `get config()` called out as one of the two code-level causes.

The base config is now a module-level shared const — components that don't override `config` no longer allocate a schema (plus its ~15 bound closures) per access. Subclass configs already return module-level `zodProps` (`netProps`, `traceProps`, …) and are unchanged.

## Scope

This intentionally does **not** attempt the Zod v4 migration or a general per-class config memo (both larger, riskier follow-ups listed in the issue). It removes the one unambiguous per-access allocation.

## Verification

- Full `tests/components` suite: 562 pass, 1 fail — the failing `registers a differential pair using port selectors` test fails identically on `main` (pre-existing, unrelated)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` / `biome check` — clean

title: Add standalone schematicsymbol element
description: Add a standalone schematicsymbol  backed by schematic-symbols, implementing it as a schematic-only PrimitiveComponent with support for explicit physical-port mapping and schematic sheetssections.
body:
## Summary

- add a standalone `<schematicsymbol />` backed by `schematic-symbols`
- implement it as a schematic-only `PrimitiveComponent`
- support explicit physical-port mapping when both `chipRef` and `connections` are provided
- support explicit schematic sheets/sections, placement, and rotation
- register the JSX intrinsic/export and bump `@tscircuit/props` to `^0.0.591`

## Connection API

`connections` maps labels exposed by `symbolName` (including `pinN` aliases) to explicit physical chip-port selectors:

```tsx
<schematicsymbol
  name="A"
  chipRef=".Q1"
  symbolName="n_channel_e_mosfet_transistor_horz"
  connections={{
    gate: "Q1.G1",
    source: "Q1.S1",
    drain: "Q1.D1",
  }}
/>

<trace from=".R1 > .pin2" to=".Q1 > .G1" />
```

The mapping does not create electrical traces. It projects the real chip ports into the symbol; normal `<trace>` elements continue to target the physical chip.

There is intentionally no automatic label matching. Supplying `chipRef` without `connections`, or `connections` without `chipRef`, emits a `source_property_ignored_warning` for the unmatched property and renders the symbol standalone. A symbol with neither remains a standalone schematic element.

## Architecture

- `SchematicSymbol` creates its own source component so the renderer displays `name` using the same `{REF}` mechanism as other components
- mapped schematic ports reuse the referenced physical chip's real `source_port_id` values
- qualified symbol names such as `_horz` and `_right` rotate through the shared `PrimitiveComponent` resolver, without a `SchematicSymbol` override
- connected components are not inferred onto a symbol's sheet; each visible component declares its own `schSheetName`
- no manual `schematic_text` insertion
- no shared `PrimitiveComponent`, `NormalComponent`, or `Port` lifecycle changes
- no PCB representation or missing-footprint behavior
- no `internalcircuit` dependency
- `displayName` rendering remains explicitly deferred until `schematic_component` has a `display_name` field

## Coverage

- standalone library symbol
- MOSFET and diode mappings with explicit connections
- two MOSFET representations (`A` and `B`) of one physical chip without a schematic sheet
- MOSFET and op-amp representations with separate traces across two explicitly assigned schematic sheets
- PCB snapshots confirming the referenced physical chips and their routed connections, without duplicate PCB components
- schematic-section participation
- warning-and-ignore behavior for incomplete `chipRef` + `connections` pairs, with no automatic port matching

## Validation

- 12 targeted schematic-symbol, symbol-rotation, and sheet regression tests pass
- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Biome checks for modified TypeScript files
- `git diff --check`
- full suite: 1,239 pass, 31 skip; one unrelated differential-pair PCB snapshot mismatch also reproduces in isolation

title: Fix nested group packing transform origin
description: Fixes incorrect transform origin for nested groups in PCB layout, preventing footprint overlap errors in TI wireless subcircuits.
body:
## Summary

- preserve the converter's initial aggregate component centers across the packing solver boundary
- use each aggregate center as the transform origin when applying packed nested-group positions
- update repro156 to assert that TI wireless subcircuits produce no footprint overlap errors
- refresh the PCB snapshot with the corrected placement

## Root cause

`convertCircuitJsonToPackOutput` expresses every descendant obstacle relative to a computed aggregate center. `convertPackOutputToPackInput` intentionally removes component centers before solving, and core then applied the packed group transform around `pcb_group.center`. For internally laid-out subcircuits that field can still be the default `(0, 0)`, so the solver's valid placement was translated from the wrong origin and the TI subcircuits overlapped.

The fix keeps the pre-solver pack output and uses its aggregate center when applying each nested-group transform, with `pcb_group.center` retained as a fallback.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repros/repro156-ti-multisheet-autolayout.test.tsx`
- `bun test tests/features/pcb-pack-layout` (12 passing)
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`
- visually inspected the refreshed repro156 PCB snapshot

title: Add repro test of footprint overlap of `tscircuit/ti` subcircuits
description: Adds a visual reproduction test for footprint overlap errors in TI subcircuits, ensuring correct packing strategies are applied and errors are asserted through PCB snapshots.

## Summary

- add a visual repro using the three `@tsci/tscircuit.ti` subcircuits from the reported circuit
- install the TI package directly from a pinned `github:tscircuit/ti` commit so public CI can reproduce it without the private scoped registry
- pass `packOrderStrategy` and `packPlacementStrategy` using the field names expected by `calculate-packing`
- assert the reported behavior through emitted `pcb_footprint_overlap_error` records and a PCB snapshot

Core previously sent the obsolete keys `orderStrategy` and `placementStrategy`. `calculate-packing` silently ignored them and used its own placement default, which caused this large nested circuit to take the wrong packing path and emit repeated solver iteration errors.

Companion fixes:

- tscircuit/calculate-packing#112 preserves unrelated shared-network connections when weighted connections exist elsewhere in the circuit.
- tscircuit/ti#85 makes the GitHub-installed TI sources compatible with core's `verbatimModuleSyntax` typecheck.

description: Fixes the issue where the allowOffBoard property was not being propagated to pcb_component for NormalComponent, Jumper, and SolderJumper, causing it to be ignored for these components.
body:
`allowOffBoard` is defined on `CommonComponentProps` and accepted by every component, but was only serialized to `pcb_component.is_allowed_to_be_off_board` by `Chip`. The base class `NormalComponent.doInitialPcbComponentRender()` and the overrides in `Jumper` and `SolderJumper` silently dropped the prop, causing `allowOffBoard` to be ignored for all non-Chip components.

This adds the missing `is_allowed_to_be_off_board: props.allowOffBoard ?? false` to all three `db.pcb_component.insert()` call sites, matching the existing pattern in `Chip`.

title: Fix zero-height mobile containers preventing 3D preview and code editor rendering
description: Fixes zero-height mobile containers that prevent the 3D preview and code editor from rendering on mobile devices.
body:
Before: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/936e68fd-8390-4b37-a64a-10bb6602907c


After: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63da030b-33dc-4447-b4de-fe65d012be13


### Motivation

The package editor’s 3D preview failed to render on mobile devices. When the responsive layout switched from a side-by-side row to a stacked column, the preview wrapper had no flexible height and collapsed to `0px`.

`SuspenseRunFrame` and its Three.js canvas depend on a non-zero parent height to calculate their rendering dimensions. As a result, the preview appeared completely blank even though the circuit loaded successfully.

The code editor was vulnerable to the same collapse when users switched to the Code view on mobile.

### Root cause

The mobile column layout relied on child containers expanding into the available vertical space, but the preview and code editor wrappers did not consistently use `flex-1`.

Their children used full-height layouts without receiving a defined height from their parents, causing the wrappers to collapse.

### User impact

Mobile users can now:

- Open a package and see its 3D preview.
- Switch between Preview and Code without either view collapsing.
- Continue using the existing desktop split layout without behavior changes.

### Reproduction

Before this fix:

1. Open a package editor on a mobile-width screen.
2. Switch to the 3D preview.
3. Observe that the preview area is blank because its wrapper has zero height.
4. Switch to the Code view and observe the same potential height collapse.

After this fix, both containers expand into the remaining vertical space and render normally.

title: Fix PR benchmark main baseline lookup
description: Fixes the issue where PR-dispatched benchmarks fail due to an empty main-dataset list, ensuring successful metadata generation and artifact download.
body:
## Summary

- provide an explicit empty main-dataset list when PR benchmarks run through `workflow_dispatch`
- download the available main benchmark artifact even if an earlier workflow step fails

## Root cause

[PR #1743](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1743) added raw benchmark metadata that requires `BENCHMARK_MAIN_DATASETS`. The dataset-loading step only runs for pushes to `main`, so PR-dispatched benchmarks received an empty value and failed before the existing main-artifact download step. Result comments then incorrectly reported that no previous main run was available.

## Impact

`/benchmark` and `/benchmark-all` PR runs can complete metadata generation and display the matching dataset from the latest successful main benchmark artifact. This changes workflow plumbing only; benchmark and solver behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- validated metadata parsing with `workflow_dispatch` using `[]`
- validated metadata parsing with the full main dataset list
- `bun test tests/main-branch-benchmark-datasets.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bun run build`
- parsed `.github/workflows/benchmark.yml` as YAML
- `git diff --check`

title: Render multi-layer obstacles with red opacity
description: Render multi-layer obstacles in red with varying opacity based on the number of layers, while keeping bottom-only obstacles blue at 50 opacity.
body:
## Summary

- render each logical obstacle exactly once instead of once per z-layer
- keep bottom-only obstacles blue at 50% opacity
- render top-only and multi-layer obstacles red, with opacity increasing by canonical layer count: `1 - 0.5^N`
- preserve compound layer metadata such as `z0,1`

This is a separate implementation based directly on `main`. It replaces the neutral-gray multi-layer treatment from #1757 with the requested layer-weighted red opacity and does not alter #1737 or #1757.

## Why the color appeared to change

The obstacle's routing layers were not being mutated. The renderer emitted coincident rectangles for every z-layer, so semi-transparent colors accumulated at the same coordinates and the final visible color depended on layer/render order. This computes the equivalent red opacity on one rectangle instead.

Examples:
- 1 top layer: red at 50%
- 2 layers: red at 75%
- 3 layers: red at 87.5%

title: Avoid duplicate obstacles for packed nested groups
description: Fixes the issue of duplicate obstacles being emitted for nested groups in PCB packing by ensuring that components already represented by a top-level packed-group aggregate are not emitted again as fixed obstacles.
body:
## Summary

- make `convertCircuitJsonToPackOutput` track PCB components already represented by a top-level packed-group aggregate
- skip fixed-obstacle emission for relatively positioned descendants already contained by that aggregate
- preserve fixed obstacles for relatively positioned components directly under the packing root
- add a focused converter regression test covering both cases

## Why

A nested group is converted into one aggregate `PackedComponent`, but its relatively positioned member components were also emitted as fixed obstacles. The solver therefore saw the same physical geometry twice: once inside the movable group and once as immovable board geometry.

The deduplication belongs at the Circuit JSON → pack-output boundary, where both representations are created and their membership is known. This is the upstream fix needed by [tscircuit/core#2808](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/2808); core should not mutate `PackOutput` after conversion.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 116 pass, 10 skip, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bunx biome check lib/plumbing/convertCircuitJsonToPackOutput.ts tests/circuit-json-pack-conversion/nested-group-obstacles.test.ts`

title: Detect and deterministically lay out crystal load-capacitor circuits
description: This PR adds explicit detection and deterministic layout for crystal oscillator circuits containing a two- or four-pin crystal, two grounded load capacitors, and an optional series resistor. Once detected, these components are grouped into a dedicated crystal_circuit partition so generic packing cannot separate them or produce an unstable arrangement. The dedicated layout solver places load capacitors relative to their corresponding crystal terminals, aligns the ground row for horizontal crystals, and places capacitors on opposite sides when the crystal is locked vertically. Developer comments explain the detection rules, ambiguity rejection, partition priority, and vertical-orientation fallback, while focused tests verify component grouping, pin alignment, optional resistor handling, and zero overlaps in the 32 kHz and RP2040 cases.
body:
This PR adds explicit detection and deterministic layout for crystal oscillator circuits containing a two- or four-pin crystal, two grounded load capacitors, and an optional series resistor. Once detected, these components are grouped into a dedicated `crystal_circuit` partition so generic packing cannot separate them or produce an unstable arrangement.

The dedicated layout solver places load capacitors relative to their corresponding crystal terminals, aligns the ground row for horizontal crystals, and places capacitors on opposite sides when the crystal is locked vertically. Developer comments explain the detection rules, ambiguity rejection, partition priority, and vertical-orientation fallback, while focused tests verify component grouping, pin alignment, optional resistor handling, and zero overlaps in the 32 kHz and RP2040 cases.

title: test: repro #687 — V1V1 net label left stacked on QD3/QCLK port labels
description: Reproduces a bug where the V1V1 net label is stacked on the QD3 and QCLK port labels due to collision resolution failure in the schematic trace solver.
body:
Reproduction-only PR for #687, as requested in the review on #690.

Input is a minimal 5-chip scene (`tests/repros/assets/repro-netlabel-collision-687.input.json`) minimized from the user-submitted board `bug-report-20260721T221026Z` (#688), preserving its exact failure mechanism and net names.

**What it shows:** the `V1V1` trace label has no strictly collision-free candidate anywhere along its trace — the pin column is walled in by the QD0–QD3/QCLK port-label column, chips above/below, and a chip closing the corridor — so `NetLabelNetLabelCollisionSolver` gives up and leaves it stacked on the `QD3` and `QCLK` port labels (total stacked overlap ≈ 0.16; the original board shows ≈ 0.168 in the same shape).

| Current behavior (pinned by this PR) |
|---|
| ![V1V1 stacked on QD3/QCLK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Hero988/schematic-trace-solver/acdb867417c44f49c74876ee250be1e3b90f9e6f/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-netlabel-collision-687.snap.svg) |

body:

Bun 1.3.1 interprets the second script name in `bun run --parallel --no-exit-on-error typecheck:files typecheck:folders` as an argument to the first script. CI consequently invokes `eslint . typecheck:folders`, and ESLint fails because no file matches that pattern.

The structure-check workflow is compatible with the Bun 1.3.1 version used by GitHub Actions while preserving fail-fast behavior between the required checks.

- `bun run build`

- `bun run typecheck:structure`

## What changed

```text
fpc12_p0.5mm_pw0.3mm_pl1.25mm_mpx8.88mm_mpy2.575mm_mpw2mm_mpl2.5mm
```

The JLC5000 95% IoU benchmark currently misclassifies these connector patterns as unrelated `tssop`, `dfn`, or `solderjumper` footprints. A dedicated family represents a missing topology and can cover multiple pin counts and pitches rather than special-casing one component.

The tests reproduce representative copper geometry from:

- JLCPCB C2856799, FPC-05F-12PH20
- JLCPCB C262505, AFC11-S30ICA-00
- JLCPCB C5343246, FPC-0.3HF-31PWBH10

This gives `circuit-json-to-footprinter` a reusable family to discover in a follow-up change.

title: Support micrometer units consistently
description: Normalizes micrometer length values to millimeters across all footprint families and numeric parameters, ensuring consistent support for micrometer units in the footprinter.
body:
## What changed

- Normalize `um` and `µm` length values to millimeters before footprint-specific parsers run.
- Apply normalization to both footprinter strings and the fluent builder API.
- Support compound dimensions such as `thermalpad2400umx3000um`.
- Add SVG snapshot coverage for simple and compound micrometer dimensions.

## Why

Micrometer support was inconsistent across footprint families. Families using the shared `circuit-json` length schema already parsed `um`, while families using `parseFloat` or `@tscircuit/mm` treated `100um` as `100mm` or rejected it. This prevented `circuit-json-to-footprinter` from safely emitting shorter sub-millimeter values.

After this change, micrometer values are equivalent to their millimeter forms across all footprint families and numeric parameters.

## Validation

title: Fix duplicate orientation canvas in StrictMode
description: Fixes a bug where a duplicate orientation canvas is created in StrictMode due to improper cleanup of effect-owned resources.
body:
## Summary

- clean up each orientation-cube effect using the exact canvas and animation frame created by that effect instance
- stop resolving effect-owned resources through mutable React refs during cleanup
- add a Strict Mode regression test that fails with two canvases before the fix and passes with one after it

## Root cause

`OrientationCubeCanvas` appends its canvas imperatively in a passive effect. During React 19 Strict Mode's effect replay, React clears the DOM ref before running the passive-effect cleanup. The cleanup guarded removal with `containerRef.current`, which was therefore `null`, so the old canvas stayed attached. When setup replayed, it appended a second canvas to the same 120×120 container. Normal document flow pushed the real orientation cube down by 120px while the orphan appeared as the broken-looking box in Runframe.

The cleanup now closes over the exact canvas, renderer, scene, camera, and animation frame created by the effect. `canvas.remove()` no longer depends on ref timing and runs before Three.js resource disposal.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/orientation-cube-strict-mode.test.tsx tests/manifold-board-textures-strict-mode.test.tsx`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- linked the built package into Runframe with its iframe Strict Mode unchanged; the orientation container contains one canvas and the stray box is gone

The repository's full test run still reports the same three unrelated failures on `main` in `preprocess-circuit-json.test.ts` and `outline-bounds.test.ts`.

title: Use schematic port IDs in the schematic trace solver
description: Fixes net-label routing when a chip and schematicbox chipRef... render the same source pin by using canonical schematic_port_id values as schematic trace-solver pin IDs end to end.
body:
## Summary

- use canonical `schematic_port_id` values as schematic trace-solver pin IDs end to end
- remove `getSchematicPortSelector` and the selector-to-port translation maps
- fix net-label routing when a `<chip>` and `<schematicbox chipRef="...">` render the same source pin
- strengthen the repro156 regression test and refresh the affected schematic snapshots

## Root cause

The trace solver used CSS-like selectors such as `U1.8` as its internal pin identity. That works while one source pin has one schematic representation.

In repro156, the chip and its schematic box both render the same source pin. Both ports therefore produced the same selector. Because the routing code stored ports in maps keyed by that selector, one rendered port overwrote the other and the net label could be routed to the wrong representation.

Each rendered schematic port already has a unique canonical `schematic_port_id`, so creating another identity from the component name and pin number was unnecessary.

## Fix

The solver now receives `schematic_port_id` directly and its output is consumed as schematic port IDs. There is no component-name suffix, port-ID suffix, or fallback selector.

The existing internally-connected-pin dedup behavior is preserved: its representative port ID is used only to detect duplicates, while the original schematic port ID is passed to the solver. The adjacent port lookup is keyed by `schematic_port_id` so separate schematic representations of one source port do not overwrite each other.

Removing `getSchematicPortSelector` only removes this internal routing identity layer. User-facing selectors such as `U1.GND` and `.pin1` still work normally; the public selector system is unchanged.

## Snapshot impact

The minimum-spanning-tree routing solver uses pin IDs to break equal-cost ties. Replacing derived selector strings with canonical port IDs can therefore select a different, but electrically equivalent, route in tied layouts. The affected schematic snapshots are refreshed accordingly.

The pushbutton internally-connected-pin snapshot is unchanged.

## Validation

- repro156 regression test passes
- `pushbutton-pin-configurations` and repro155 internally-connected-pin tests pass
- relevant schematic trace and section tests pass
- TypeScript typecheck passes
- package build passes

title: fix: propagate manufacturerPartNumber and supplierPartNumbers in transistor, crystal, fuse, potentiometer, and interconnect
description: Fixes the issue where manufacturerPartNumber and supplierPartNumbers were not being propagated to the source_component for several components, causing them to be omitted from the BOM.
body:
Fixes #2787

## Problem

`<transistor />`, `<crystal />`, `<fuse />`, `<potentiometer />`, and `<interconnect />` accept `supplierPartNumbers` and `manufacturerPartNumber` (valid per their props, which extend `CommonComponentProps`), but each component's `doInitialSourceRender()` builds the `source_component` with a fixed field list that omits `supplier_part_numbers` and `manufacturer_part_number`. The values silently disappear and the parts never reach the BOM — no type error, no warning.

Same defect as the `<switch />` fix (tscircuit#4056 → #2765) and the `<mosfet />` fix (#2776 → #2778). Found by auditing every `db.source_component.insert` call site in `lib/` for the missing fields after those merges; these five are the remaining affected components (`EnclosureFdmBox` also omits the fields but its props reject them, so it is excluded).

## Fix

Pass both fields through in each `doInitialSourceRender()`, matching the pattern used by the other normal components (`manufacturerPartNumber ?? mfn` alias handling as in Resistor/Switch/Mosfet):

```ts
manufacturer_part_number: props.manufacturerPartNumber ?? props.mfn,
supplier_part_numbers: props.supplierPartNumbers,
```

Two lines per component; Interconnect additionally gets the same `const { _parsedProps: props } = this` destructure the others already use.

## Test

Red→green tests in `tests/components/normal-components/supplier-part-numbers-propagation.test.tsx` — one per component, each rendering the component with a real JLCPCB part (MMBT3904/C20526, X322516MLB4SI/C13738, SMD1206P050TF/C20799, 3296W-1-103LF/C34846, 0603WAF0000T5E/C21189) and asserting both fields land on the `source_component`. All five fail on main (`undefined`), all pass with this change. Full `bun test` suite, `tsc --noEmit`, and `biome format` clean.

title: fix: align transistor pin aliases/accessors with schematic-symbols (pin1=collector, pin2=base, pin3=emitter)
description: Fixes incorrect transistor pin aliases and accessors to align with schematic symbols, resolving issues in SPICE netlist generation.
body:
Fixes tscircuit/tscircuit#3617

## Root cause

The `schematic-symbols` package numbers the BJT ports as **pin1 = collector, pin2 = base, pin3 = emitter** — identically for `npn_bipolar_transistor` and `pnp_bipolar_transistor`, in both `_horz` and `_vert` orientations (verified against the currently-pinned `schematic-symbols@0.0.232`):

```
npn_bipolar_transistor_horz / pnp_bipolar_transistor_horz:
  ["1","collector"]  x=-0.55  y= 0.29
  ["2","base"]       x= 0.00  y=-0.40
  ["3","emitter"]    x= 0.55  y= 0.29
```

`Transistor.ts` disagreed with this in two places at once:

```ts
// aliases said pin2=emitter, pin3=base (symbol says pin2=base, pin3=emitter)
pin1: ["collector", "c"], pin2: ["emitter", "e"], pin3: ["base", "b"]

// and the accessors even disagreed with the aliases directly above them
emitter = this.portMap.pin1   // pin1 is aliased "collector"!
collector = this.portMap.pin2
base = this.portMap.pin3
```

Because schematic positions are assigned by pin number, ports ended up with **contradictory port_hints** — e.g. pin2 carried both `"base"` (from the symbol) and `"emitter"` (from the alias) — so name-based selectors and downstream consumers resolved pins arbitrarily.

## This was corrupting SPICE netlists, not just symbol positions

`circuit-json-to-spice` resolves BJT terminals by port hints. With the contradictory hints, the switch-circuit test (`ngspice-spice-analysis01-switch`) generated:

```
before:  SSW1 N2 0 ...      ← switch output shorted to ground
         QQ1  N3 0 0 NPN    ← base AND emitter both on node 0 (B-E short, transistor can never turn on)
after:   SSW1 N2 N3 ...
         QQ1  N4 N3 0 NPN   ← collector=N4, base=N3, emitter=GND — correct
```

The old simulation snapshot showed a flat collector voltage (transistor permanently off); the updated snapshot shows the correct 0↔5 V switching waveform. That's why the two snapshot updates in this PR are part of the fix, not incidental churn.

## Answers to the questions raised on the earlier attempts (props#698, props#714, core#2541 — all stale-closed)

- **@imrishabh18 "Wouldn't this mess up the PNP mapping?"** — No: the PNP symbol uses the *same* numbering as NPN (`pin1=collector, pin2=base, pin3=emitter`, verified above), so one mapping fixes both. The new test asserts positions for **both** npn and pnp.
- **@ShiboSoftwareDev "is this consistent within the repo?"** — Both BJT symbol variants and both orientations agree. MOSFET/JFET symbols use their own gate/source/drain labels and are untouched by this change (the `Mosfet` component has its own mapping; `mosfet-symbol-port-sides.test.tsx` still passes).
- Note the earlier core attempt (#2541) proposed `pin2=emitter`, which contradicts the symbols package — merging it would have swapped base and emitter.

## Changes

- `Transistor.ts`: aliases → `pin1: ["collector","c"], pin2: ["base","b"], pin3: ["emitter","e"]`; accessors → `collector=pin1, base=pin2, emitter=pin3`.
- `transistor-ports.test.tsx`: two new tests — (1) the schematic port named collector/base/emitter must sit at the symbol port with that label, for npn **and** pnp (red on `main`: 2 fail → green here); (2) accessors must match the aliases.
- Regenerated the two affected snapshots (schematic layout + the now-physically-correct ngspice switch simulation).

Ran `tsc --noEmit` (clean), `biome check` (clean), and every test file referencing transistors (12 pass / 0 fail), plus the spice-analysis suite.

A follow-up PR to `props` aligning `transistorPins` (`pin1=emitter, pin2=collector` there today) with the same order is ready; it's independent of this fix.

---

title: Reuse schematic symbol ports for trace routing
description: Refactors schematic routing to reuse existing schematic symbol ports for trace routing, improving efficiency and clarity in the routing process.
body:
## Summary

This is a cleaner alternative to #2775 and #2768.

- add one helper that returns the physical port supplying a pin's existing schematic symbol port
- keep the first physical pin for each shared schematic symbol port when building one named-net solver input
- mark all physical pins using a routed schematic symbol port as connected
- preserve all physical `schematic_port` and `source_trace` records
- use distinct branded `SchematicPortId` and `SourcePortId` types throughout schematic routing
- avoid coordinate matching
- add regression assertions for both visible labels, exact GND trace termination, and connected physical GND pins

## Why this is cleaner

The component has already assigned `schematicSymbolPortDef` before schematic routing starts. The routing code can use that assignment directly.

Unlike #2775, this version does not build a port-ID map in the solver input and pass it through the schematic render orchestration to the output step. Both routing stages call the same small helper instead.

Pins using different schematic symbol ports remain separate, even when electrically internally connected. Explicitly positioned ports and imported Circuit JSON ports also remain separate.

The branded IDs prevent source-port and schematic-port identifiers from being mixed inside routing sets and maps. The conversion from Circuit JSON's current string fields happens only at the routing boundary.

## Validation

- focused pushbutton reproduction and corrected schematic snapshot
- existing pushbutton configurations with different named nets
- related ATmega328P, RP2040, jumper, solder-jumper, net-label, and elbow-routing tests
- multi-sheet schematic tests
- imported Circuit JSON regression
- `bunx biome check ...`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

The broad local run encountered host-load timeouts in unrelated autorouting tests. The long Arduino rerouting test passed alone, and the auto-jumper timeout reproduced on the untouched reproduction branch.

title: Apply crystal trace limits through routing DRC
description: Implements maximum trace length constraints for crystal components during design rule checks, ensuring stricter adherence to trace length limits for connected components.
body:
## Summary
- make `Crystal` own its default/configured maximum trace-length behavior
- apply the limit in `Crystal.doInitialSourceDesignRuleChecks()`, immediately after connectivity-map keys are generated
- constrain direct crystal traces plus MCU and load-capacitor branches on the same nets
- preserve stricter per-trace constraints, such as capacitor decoupling limits
- remove crystal-specific propagation from `Group` and generic `Trace` utilities
- remove the bespoke `insertPcbTraceTooLongWarnings` mutation path

## Architecture
Core tees up Circuit JSON from the owning component: each crystal writes the effective constraint to matching `source_trace.max_length` records during the source DRC phase. The normal board `runDrcChecks` → `runAllRoutingChecks` pipeline then emits `pcb_trace_too_long_warning` elements through the generic check released from tscircuit/checks#174.

This PR now depends on the published `@tscircuit/checks@0.0.146` release containing that generic check.

## Validation

- configured crystal limits preserve stricter capacitor limits

title: Support schSectionName on schematic boxes
description: Adds support for schSectionName on schematic boxes, allowing chip-backed schematic boxes to be associated with specific sections in the schematic trace solver.
body:
## Summary

- update `@tscircuit/props` to `0.0.590`, which adds `schSectionName` to `<schematicbox />`
- key schematic trace-solver section membership by rendered `schematic_component_id` instead of source component name
- add a regression test and schematic snapshot covering two sectioned schematic-box representations of the same source chip

Depends on and follows [tscircuit/props#750](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/750), which is merged and published in `@tscircuit/props@0.0.590`.

## Why

A chip-backed `<schematicbox>` creates its own rendered schematic component while referencing another component's source identity. Core previously derived trace-solver sections through source component names, so schematic boxes named `U1 Power` and `U1 I/O` both reached the solver without a `sectionId` when they represented source chip `U1`.

Associating sections with the rendered schematic component preserves the existing behavior for normal components and also allows multiple schematic representations of one source chip to belong to different sections.

## Impact

`schSectionName` now reaches the schematic trace solver for chip-backed schematic boxes, keeping their routing scoped to the intended section. Existing `schSheetName` support remains unchanged.

## Validation

- regression test failed before the implementation with both section IDs `undefined`, then passed after the change

title: Add bus types to SimpleRouteJson
description: Adds a new SimpleRouteBus type to the SimpleRouteJson representation, allowing for bus metadata to be preserved during preprocessing without altering routing behavior.
body:
## Summary

- make `lib/types/srj-types.ts` the canonical public source for the SimpleRouteJson type family
- stop re-exporting or intersecting SimpleRouteJson and SimplifiedPcbTrace from `high-density-repair03`
- preserve the previously exposed SRJ surface locally, including `zLayers`, connection root metadata, via-to-pad clearance, and terminal wire port IDs
- normalize public `zLayers` into the autorouter's internal `__zLayers` representation
- add a `SimpleRouteBus` type with `busId`, ordered `connectionNames`, and optional `maxLengthSkew`
- verify public bus metadata survives preprocessing

```ts
buses: [
  {
    busId: "data",
    connectionNames: ["data0", "data1", "data2"],
    maxLengthSkew: 0.1,
  },
]
```

## Ownership

`@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` now defines and exports its own SRJ types. `high-density-repair03` remains an implementation dependency for DRC repair, but it no longer supplies the autorouter package's public SimpleRouteJson definition.

## Scope

This PR proposes the SRJ representation only. It does not add bus length-matching behavior, change routing, or alter via-in-pad defaults.

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`

title: Scope weighted connection filtering to participating pads
description: Scope weighted connection filtering to pads that actually participate in weighted metadata, ensuring that only explicitly listed pad pairs are eligible for placement scoring while preserving normal same-network fallback for unrelated unweighted pads.
body:
## Summary

- scope weighted-connection filtering to pads that actually participate in weighted metadata
- keep explicitly listed pad pairs eligible for placement scoring
- preserve normal same-network fallback for unrelated unweighted pads
- continue rejecting unlisted alternatives for pads whose weighted connection sets `ignoreWeakConnections: true`
- update the three visual snapshots whose ordinary same-net passives now influence placement

## Why

Previously, adding any `weightedConnections` entry changed the list into a global allowlist. A direct connection hint for one pair therefore made every unlisted pair in the entire pack input weak, including unrelated chip-to-passive connections. That removed most passive proximity targets and contributed to linear-looking packing.

This change does **not** make every electrical connection strong. Callers first require matching `networkId`, then this helper applies the following policy:

| Pair | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Explicitly listed together | considered |
| Neither pad appears in weighted metadata | considered through the normal same-network fallback |
| Either pad participates in an `ignoreWeakConnections: true` entry, but the pair is unlisted | ignored |
| Participating entry allows weak connections | considered through the same-network fallback |

The numeric `weight` field is unchanged; this PR only fixes which same-network targets are eligible.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 120 pass, 10 skip, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bunx biome check lib/utils/isStrongConnection.ts tests/is-strong-connection.test.ts`
- `tests/repros/repro156-ti-multisheet-autolayout.test.ts` passes in the full suite

title: Support schematic port IDs in net label grouping
description: Fixes net label grouping by resolving opaque pin IDs to their owning chips, ensuring uniform GND rail behavior in schematic outputs.
body:
## Summary

- resolve opaque pin IDs such as `schematic_port_29` to their owning chip through `InputProblem.chips`
- retain historical merged-group IDs for legacy component-qualified pins such as `J2.13`
- add a focused unit test for schematic-port grouping
- add the exact current `@tscircuit/core` RP2040 gamepad solver input and a visual regression proving uniform GND rails

## Root cause

`groupLabelsByChipAndOrientation` inferred component ownership with `pinId.split(".")[0]`. That worked for legacy IDs such as `J2.13`, but Core now passes schematic port IDs such as `schematic_port_29`, which contain no component prefix. Every port was therefore treated as a separate component during netlabel merging.

Because adjacent labels were not merged into component-side obstacles, the trace/label overlap stage rerouted individual GND branches around separate labels. Those detours produced the staggered rails seen in Core even with schematic-trace-solver 0.0.109.

The fix uses the chip/pin relationship already present in the solver input as the source of truth for opaque IDs. The prior cleanup-stage workaround has been removed from the final diff.

## Impact

Current Core output with schematic-port IDs now follows the same component-side label grouping behavior as legacy component-qualified pin IDs. The RP2040 repro produces one uniform GND rail on each side of the chip without weakening rail-alignment readability checks.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 146 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- focused trace-label overlap and RP2040 tests — 10 passed, 0 failed

title: Emit compact 10 µm footprint dimensions
description: Rounds generated footprint dimensions to the nearest 10 m and emits positive dimensions below 0.1 mm as integer um values, while keeping larger dimensions in mm form.
body:
## What changed

- Round generated footprint dimensions to the nearest 10 µm (0.01 mm).
- Emit positive dimensions below 0.1 mm as integer `um` values.
- Keep dimensions at or above 0.1 mm in concise `mm` form.
- Apply the same quantization to optimized parameters, generated seeds, and compound thermal-pad dimensions.

For example, `0.05mm` becomes `50um`, while `0.1mm`, `0.55mm`, and larger dimensions remain in millimeters.

## Why

The formatter previously emitted up to four decimal places followed by `mm`, producing unnecessarily long strings and precision below what footprint matching needs. Integer micrometer values are shorter for very small dimensions, and 10 µm resolution keeps the geometry within the intended tolerance without making common sub-millimeter values less readable.

## Dependency

This PR depends on [tscircuit/footprinter#729](https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/pull/729), which makes `um` parsing consistent across all footprint families, fluent-builder parameters, and compound dimensions. The formatter suite passes with its current declared dependency; full cross-family compatibility was additionally validated against the linked footprinter branch. The dependency should be bumped to the released footprinter version before this PR merges.

## What changed

## Why

The existing `pinrow*_smd` layout places every pad on one centerline. Vertical single-row SMT male headers use alternating solder tails, so they need a distinct land pattern.

The defaults follow the [Harwin M20-877R recommended pad layout](https://content.harwin.com/asset/08a71c70-ecf2-488d-b460-84a3db4226fe/DRG-00411-Technical-Drawing-Datasheet-M20-877R-pdf.pdf): 2.54 mm contact pitch, 5.82 mm overall land-pattern height, 1.00 x 2.51 mm pads, and therefore 3.31 mm between alternating pad-row centers.

title: Make Matchpack layout failures nonfatal
description: Stops throwing an execution error when the Matchpack solver reports failure and records a non-fatal schematic layout error instead.
body:
## What changed

- Stops throwing an execution error when the Matchpack solver reports failure.
- Records a `schematic_layout_error` with `is_fatal: false` and the original solver error in its message.
- Returns from the layout phase without applying any replacement placement, leaving existing schematic positions untouched.
- Converts repro159 from `test.failing` into a normal passing schematic snapshot regression.

## Why

Repro159 creates a 146-component strong-connection partition from the XIAO, series resistor, and 144-LED data chain. PackSolver2 is still making progress when it reaches its fixed 100,000-iteration ceiling, but core currently throws and aborts the entire circuit render.

Automatic schematic layout failure should be represented in Circuit JSON rather than preventing Circuit JSON from being produced.

## Impact

Circuits that exhaust Matchpack's iteration budget now finish rendering and expose a non-fatal `schematic_layout_error`. This change deliberately does not introduce a secondary layout algorithm or alter component positions after Matchpack fails.

## Validation

title: Add WLED matrix Matchpack iteration repro
description: Adds a reduced reproduction of a 1212 WLED matrix circuit to document a known Matchpack layout solver failure without affecting CI.
body:
## What changed

Adds `repro159`, a reduced reproduction of a 12×12 WLED matrix circuit. It preserves the schematic topology from the reported circuit—144 four-pin WLED chips, a chained data path, shared 5 V and GND rails, a XIAO ESP32-C3, series resistor, bulk capacitor, and 12 row decoupling capacitors—while omitting PCB-only footprint and placement detail.

## Why

Rendering this circuit currently fails during initial schematic Matchpack layout:

```text
Matchpack layout solver failed: Partition 0 failed: PackSolver2 failed: PackSolver2 ran out of iterations
```

The repro uses Bun's `test.failing` so the known solver failure is exercised and documented without making CI red. Once the solver issue is fixed, the test should be changed back to a normal `test` and a schematic snapshot can be recorded.

## Impact

Provides a focused regression case for large, highly connected LED matrices without involving PCB routing or detailed imported footprint geometry.

description: Fixes junction creation logic to prevent junctions between traces of different nets in schematic rendering.

- add a focused CC2/GND regression plus a same-net control

title: Pass fallback net label widths to schematic trace solver
description: Fixes the fallback net label width used by the schematic trace solver to match the rendered width of the label in the schematic, ensuring accurate routing.
body:
## Summary

- resolve the same fallback net-label text that Core renders for long schematic connections
- measure that rendered label and pass its width through `InputDirectConnection.netLabelWidth`
- add a repro119 assertion for the `U1_pin4` width and update affected routing snapshots

## Why this belongs in Core

The schematic trace solver already accepts `netLabelWidth`, but Core only populated it for explicit trace labels. Generated fallback labels such as `U1_pin4` were therefore routed using the solver's placeholder width (0.45) even though Core rendered a 0.96-wide label. Passing the rendered width at the input boundary keeps the solver generic and makes routing match Core's actual output.

## Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format`

title: Restore schematic pin stubs inside text-expanded bounds
description: Restores internal pin stubs when the trace solver projects a schematic port to a text-expanded component boundary, ensuring proper connection of pins that were previously omitted due to expanded text boundaries.
body:
## Summary

- restores internal pin stubs when the trace solver projects a schematic port to a text-expanded component boundary
- preserves the existing short-gap pin snapping behavior
- uses the component's expanded `Bounds` as the source of truth when the projected gap exceeds the legacy 1.5-unit cutoff
- uses `Bounds` and `pointToBoundsDistance` from `@tscircuit/math-utils`
- updates the reproduction snapshot to show `Q_USB_BOOST_OFF` connected at its base

## Root cause

The trace was not removed. Long reference-designator text expands the transistor's routing obstacle, placing the real base pin inside that obstacle. The solver intentionally projects that port to the obstacle boundary and emits the external route, while core is responsible for adding the short internal segment back to the real pin.

Core previously added that segment only when the projected endpoint was within the arbitrary `MAX_PIN_SNAP_GAP` of 1.5. The reproduction's endpoint-to-pin gap is 1.7, so core omitted the internal stub and made the otherwise-present trace look disconnected.

## Approach

Keep the existing text-aware solver input and normal near-pin correction. For gaps larger than 1.5, reconnect an endpoint only when it:

- belongs to a routed schematic port
- is axis-aligned with the real pin
- lies on or inside that port's text-expanded component bounds

This fixes text-expanded pins without changing the established handling of smaller solver-to-pin gaps.

## Reproduction

The reproduction was added separately in #2820.

## Validation

- 24 focused schematic routing, text-bounds, junction, and regression tests passed
- both tests that caught the first revision in CI now pass locally:
  - `RP2040 auto-layout with schematic sections`
  - `polarized capacitor schOrientation`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx @biomejs/biome check lib/components/primitive-components/Group/Group_doInitialSchematicTraceRender/applyTracesFromSolverOutput.ts tests/repros/repro157-three-way-transistor-base-junction.test.tsx`

## Summary

title: add vertical SMD pin header model
description: Add a configurable SmdPinHeader JSCAD model with vertical square posts and alternating SMD tails, integrating it with Footprinter3d and providing an interactive example and snapshot test.
body:
## Summary

- add a configurable `SmdPinHeader` JSCAD model with vertical square posts and alternating SMD tails
- integrate `smdpinheader*` Footprinter strings with `Footprinter3d`
- add an interactive example and a six-pin PNG snapshot test
- update `@tscircuit/footprinter` to `0.0.392`, the first published version containing `smdpinheader`

## Why

The existing SMD `PinRow` model represents a right-angle header with all tails on one side. Vertical surface-mount pin headers use upright mating posts with alternating solder tails, so they need distinct geometry.

The default dimensions follow the Harwin M20-877R family: 2.54 mm contact pitch, 0.64 mm square pins, 2.50 × 2.54 mm insulator, 1.27 mm standoff, 5.8 mm mating posts, and a 5.08 mm physical tail span. The example uses `smdpinheader6_py3.31mm`, matching the corrected land-pattern center spacing from tscircuit/footprinter#740.

## Validation

body:
## Summary

- add a parameter-driven `FPC` connector model for Footprinter's new `fpc` primitive
- model the dark LCP housing, ivory locking actuator, open cable throat, individual spring contacts, SMT tails, hinge ears, and stamped-metal hold-downs
- support pin count, pitch, stagger/reverse layout, contact sizes, and mounting-pad placement
- wire the model through `Footprinter3d`, export it, and add a Cosmos example
- add committed visual regression snapshots from angled, top, bottom, and left viewpoints
- bump Footprinter to `^0.0.391`

## Reference comparison

The default `fpc12` geometry is based on the exact footprint source part: [XUNPU FPC-05F-12PH20 / LCSC C2856799](https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C2856799.html) and the [manufacturer product listing](https://www.xunpu.com.cn/product/412.html).

For 12 pins, the datasheet calls out a 0.5 mm pitch, 10.40 mm overall width, 5.12 mm depth, and 2.00 mm mounted height. Its material table specifies LCP for the body and lock, with tin-plated phosphor-bronze contacts and solder tabs. Product photography was used to match the dark housing, ivory actuator, exposed contact teeth, end hinges, and side hold-down proportions.

title: Limit homepage cache to one hour
description: Limits the homepage cache duration to one hour, ensuring users receive the latest content after deployment without relying on long-lived KV cache.
body:
## Summary

- bypass the long-lived KV cache for the homepage
- cache homepage responses in browsers/shared caches for one hour with `must-revalidate`
- preserve `cachebust=1` as a `no-store` response
- leave existing API and list-route cache behavior unchanged

## Root cause

The homepage used the generic D1 response cache, which treats KV entries as fresh for 14 days and retains stale entries for up to 30 days. Each cached response also advertised a fresh 14-day HTTP cache window. Deploying new homepage markup did not invalidate the canonical KV entry, so users could continue receiving old HTML until manually requesting `cachebust=1`.

## Impact

New homepage responses can remain cached for at most one hour and must be revalidated afterward. Because the homepage is rendered directly from deployed code, bypassing KV also ensures a deployment is not hidden behind an older server-side homepage entry.

Existing browsers that already stored the previous 14-day response may require one final hard refresh after deployment.

## Validation

- `bunx vitest run` — 137 tests passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx @biomejs/biome@1.9.4 check cf-proxy/src/index.ts cf-proxy/test/worker.test.ts`

title: Avoid overlaps from generated net-label traces
description: Fixes overlap issues between generated net-label traces and existing ground traces in the schematic trace solver.
body: ## ISSUE ## Summary - rebase onto the merged RP2040 USB-C repro from #728 - rerun overlap resolution after `AvailableNetOrientationSolver` creates connector traces - constrain that late pass so only generated `available-net-orientation-*` traces may move - update the merged repro assertion from the two known GND overlaps to no cross-net collinear overlaps ## Root cause The pipeline resolved cross-net trace overlaps before net-label orientation correction. `AvailableNetOrientationSolver` then added the CC2 connector later, so that generated connector never went through overlap resolution and landed directly on two GND traces. The long U-shaped trace highlighted in the repro is legitimate: it is `schematic_port_94-schematic_port_92`, the GND connection from R9’s downward-facing bottom pin to R8’s downward-facing bottom pin. A straight segment would cross both resistor bodies, so the line solver routes below R9, along the component-clearance boundary, and back into R8 from below. The revised fix preserves that established GND route and shifts only the generated CC2 connector with endpoint-preserving terminal jogs. ## Tests No additional repro test is added by this branch; it modifies the merged #728 test and snapshot. Two existing snapshots containing the same generated-label overlap behavior are refreshed. ## Related Complements tscircuit/core#2878, which prevents different-net trace contacts from being rendered as electrical junctions. ## Validation - `bun test` — 147 passed, 4 skipped - `bunx tsc --noEmit` - `bun run format:check`

title: Prefer adaptive elbows for short backtracking routes
description: Prefer the adaptive elbow when a fixed-overshoot route between inward-facing pins backtracks, while retaining the default elbow for non-backtracking routes and preserving existing adaptive-on-collision behavior.
body:
## Summary

- prefer the adaptive elbow when a fixed-overshoot route between inward-facing pins backtracks
- retain the default elbow for non-backtracking routes and preserve the existing adaptive-on-collision behavior
- add a pin-level regression using the core repro47 D2/SW2 geometry, plus a solver SVG snapshot

## Root cause

Core's `repro47-switch-matrix-diodes` circuit places several diode cathodes about 0.26 schematic units from their switch pins. The default elbow uses a fixed 0.2-unit overshoot from both endpoints, so its legs pass one another and produce a 0.64-unit serpentine. Because that route is collision-free, the existing collision fallback never selects the shorter adaptive elbow.

The new predicate selects the adaptive path only when the pins face each other, the default route backtracks, the adaptive path is shorter, and the adaptive path is collision-free.

## Core repro47 before/after

These are the full schematic snapshots from `tests/repros/repro47-switch-matrix-diodes.test.tsx`. The before image is core `main`; the after image is byte-for-byte identical to the snapshot rendered from clean core `main` with this locally built solver branch.

### Before

![Core repro47 before — serpentine diode-to-switch traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/46d5ae90cc4071045ffdc0a76a3db48fdc1d5be3/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro47-switch-matrix-diodes-schematic.snap.svg)

### After

![Core repro47 after — compact diode-to-switch traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/9f61480de5f60dae5da2ff5df5e0c160ab99d1b4/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro47-switch-matrix-diodes-schematic.snap.svg)

## Validation

title: Fix stacked GND rail label orientation
description: Fixes the orientation of stacked GND rail labels to ensure they are rendered correctly between connected components.
body: ### BEFORE ### AFTER ![Core repro84 schematic after the solver fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/327e0a11687dfdffbc079ebd73633d0ec475ff50/pr-assets/repro84-core-after-solver-fix.svg) ## Summary - consider every connected component when calculating lateral orientation-search distance for single-direction vertical rail labels - allow the stacked-component GND connection to reach the requested `y-` rail orientation and add the required connector trace - add a focused repro84 regression test without changing unrelated signal-label routing snapshots ## Root cause For labels constrained to a vertical rail orientation (`y+` or `y-`), `AvailableNetOrientationSolver` derived its lateral search limit from only the first connected pin's component. When that component was on the opposite side of the requested direction, the search distance could be zero even though another connected component was the obstacle that needed to be cleared. The solver then kept its fallback side-facing label, which core rendered as plain `GND` text instead of the ground rail symbol. ## Validation - `bun test` — 145 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed - `bunx tsc --noEmit` - `bun run format:check` - ran the captured core repro84 solver input and confirmed all four GND labels resolve to `y-` ## Core integration snapshot

title: Fix RP2040 schematic placement
description: Fixes schematic section naming for the RP2040 microcontroller to allow multiple instances to share a sheet safely and improves component placement for USB-C and QSPI flash symbols.
body:
## Summary

- update the development stack to `tscircuit@0.0.2153` / `@tscircuit/core@0.0.1521`
- define the RP2040 controller's four schematic sections inside `<Microcontroller_RP2040 />`
- scope internal section names by subcircuit instance so multiple RP2040s can share a sheet safely

- give the USB-C and QSPI flash symbols explicit pin arrangements and usable dimensions
- let the built-in section layout place flash, USB, clock, and power decoupling components near their connected targets
- arrange the six RP2040 IOVDD decouplers as a clean single-row parallel bank
- add sheet-ownership and decoupling-layout regression coverage

## Why

`@tscircuit/core` PR #2780 now lets schematic sections declared inside a subcircuit inherit the sheet assigned to that subcircuit. That means boards importing `<Microcontroller_RP2040 />` no longer need to redeclare its internal sections. The reusable component owns its schematic structure while the consumer only selects the sheet. Its six IOVDD decouplers form one conventional V3V3-to-GND parallel bank below the RP2040, clear of the GPIO labels.

PCB placement and routing are unchanged.

title: Discover round through-hole footprints
description: Fixes the handling of circular drill rotations in footprint generation, allowing for accurate representation of round through-hole components like DIP ICs and bridge rectifiers.
body:
## Summary

- treat circular drill rotation as geometrically irrelevant when encoding rotated matches
- generate DIP seeds without square pin-one plating for all-round plated-hole targets
- initialize DIP width from pad-center spacing instead of total outer-copper bounds
- add real JLCPCB regressions for a rotated DIP, bridge rectifier, and HC-49 crystal
- add and visually inspect an SVG snapshot of the rotated all-round DIP

## Root cause

Rotated candidates with circular drills were rejected because their numerically different hole rotations were compared even though circles are rotationally invariant. All-round imported footprints also lacked a DIP seed without square pin-one copper. Finally, the DIP width optimizer started from the total copper bounds instead of the distance between pad centers.

body:
## Summary

- regenerate `obstacle-dataset01` from complete, DRC-clean A03 reference routes
- keep the first half of each completed route as immutable obstacles and ask B01 to route only the removed connections
- require every original connection in benchmark output and validate intersections across the unchanged preroutes and newly routed traces
- record the full-routability invariant in dataset format version 2
- add a Vercel-hosted Cosmos fixture for interactively browsing and solving all 100 obstacle samples

## Root cause

The previous generator independently routed only the obstacle half. That proved the selected half was routable by itself, but it did not prove those exact obstacle traces could coexist with the withheld connections. In particular, the old sample set included a source problem that A03 could not route as a complete node.

The corrected generator first solves and geometry-validates the entire source node. It then selects half of that completed route as obstacles. Therefore the exact immutable obstacle traces are known to have a valid completion.

## Fixed-obstacle behavior

B01 does not thaw, replace, or reroute obstacles. The benchmark passes only the removed connection ports to B01, combines its output with the original obstacle objects, checks that every original connection is present, and runs combined relaxed-DRC geometry validation.

## Cosmos preview

[Open obstacle-dataset01 sample browser](https://high-density-b01-git-agent-b01-selective-thaw-tscircuit.vercel.app/?fixture=%7B%22path%22%3A%22fixtures%2Fobstacle-dataset01%2Fobstacle-dataset01-selector.fixture.tsx%22%7D)

The fixture supports sample-number input plus previous/next navigation across all 100 samples. Immutable obstacle traces are dashed, B01 output traces are solid, and colors indicate copper layers.

- relaxed-DRC valid: 100/100
- geometry violations: 0
- P50: 0.007s
- P95: 0.076s
- average: 0.017s
- average iterations: 1,315

body:
## Summary

- add `HighDensitySolverB01`, derived from A03, with layer-aware pre-routed trace and via obstacles loaded into the routing hypergraph
- preserve same-root connectivity while blocking foreign-root copper
- use per-cell obstacle ownership as a broad phase and exact collision checks in output coordinates to avoid oversized coarse-grid obstacle approximations
- enforce the B01 routing-window limit at 15×15mm
- persist obstacle root connection names in `obstacle-dataset01`
- make the root benchmark run the 100-sample obstacle dataset while retaining the inherited Z04 benchmark as `bun run benchmark:z04`

## Behavior

This first B01 milestone treats supplied obstacles as frozen. On the full obstacle dataset it solves and validates 68/100 samples. Every completed sample has zero combined pre-routed/new-route geometry violations.

The remaining failures define the selective-thaw follow-up: because the dataset routes only one half of the connections, a frozen route can occupy a withheld connection's port shadow. Those cases cannot be solved correctly until the conflicting frozen route is released and rerouted.

## Benchmark

`./benchmark.sh --concurrency 4 --max-iterations 1000000 --stats`

- valid: 68/100
- P50: 0.008s
- P95: 0.237s
- average: 0.069s
- wall time: 2.278s

## Summary

- resolve bus trace names or port selectors to routing-scope SRJ connection names
- emit bus membership through `SimpleRouteJson.buses`
- add visual regression tests for both supported authoring forms

## Why

The autorouter boundary currently carries individual connections and differential-pair constraints, but it cannot preserve higher-level bus membership. Without that metadata, routers cannot intentionally order or attract related BGA breakout traces.

```ts
{
  buses: [
    {
      name: "DATA",
      connectionNames: ["source_trace_0", "source_trace_1"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Authors can identify members with trace names or port selectors such as `.U1 > .pin1`.

title: Fix sponsorship identity matching and incomplete weeks
description: Fixes sponsorship identity matching for contributors with mixed legacy and ID-backed records, ensuring accurate sponsorship calculations and excluding incomplete weeks until their reporting cutoff.
body:
## Summary

- bridge pre-ID weekly overview records to an ID-backed contributor when the same login has exactly one durable identity in the month
- keep the compatibility behavior local to sponsorship generation and avoid guessing when a login maps to multiple IDs
- exclude active overview weeks until their Tuesday 18:00 UTC reporting cutoff has passed
- add regression tests for mixed legacy/ID-backed records and incomplete weeks
- regenerate the July 2026 sponsorship CSV without duplicate usernames

## Root cause

PR #346 changed sponsorship aggregation from username keys to durable identity keys. Weekly overviews generated before that change resolve to `login:<username>`, while newer overviews resolve to `github:<id>`. A month spanning both formats therefore created two sponsorship entries for the same unchanged login.

The sponsorship week selector also compared the overview's display end date at midnight with the current time. Current overview files begin at a Tuesday cutoff and remain active until the following Tuesday at 18:00 UTC, so the selector could count an unfinished week early.

## Impact

This provides migration compatibility for mixed-format months without weakening ID-based identity handling elsewhere. Legacy records are only bridged when an ID-bearing record supplies an unambiguous match for the same normalized login. Sponsorship calculations now stop at the latest completed reporting week.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 45 passing
- `bun run format:check`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun scripts/generate-sponsorship-csv.ts 2026 7` — 3 completed weeks, 11 sponsorships, total `$6,760`
- verified the regenerated CSV contains zero duplicate usernames

This workflow applies schema migrations only. Derived-table data synchronization remains separate because `sync-db.sh` requires a prepared local database source.

title: fix: add support for Greek small letter mu (U+03BC) alongside micro sign (U+00B5) in unit parsing
description: Fixes silent parsing vulnerability where Greek Small Letter Mu (U03BC) was incorrectly evaluated as unitless instead of as a micro prefix in unit parsing.
body:
## Description

This PR fixes a silent parsing vulnerability across tscircuit where electrical values containing the standard Greek Small Letter Mu (`μ`, `U+03BC`) were mistakenly evaluated as unitless base magnitudes (e.g., Henrys, Farads, Amperes) rather than micro prefixes.

## Root Cause & Issue Fixed

In Unicode, there are two distinct code points that look visually identical to end-users and documentation authors:
1. **`µ` (`U+00B5`, Micro Sign):** Previously supported by `format-si-unit`.
2. **`μ` (`U+03BC`, Greek Small Letter Mu):** Commonly produced by keyboard layouts and documentation generators, but entirely unhandled in prefix lookup and variant mapping tables.

Because `format-si-unit` lacked `U+03BC` in `SI_PREFIX_VALUES` and unit variant dictionaries, when an engineer or documentation code runner passed `inductance="10μH"`, the unit converter discarded the unrecognized character and mistakenly evaluated the element as a massive **10 Henrys (`10H`)** instead of **10 microhenrys (`10µH`)**.

## Changes Made
- Added explicit Greek Mu (`μ`, `U+03BC`) support alongside existing Micro Sign (`µ`, `U+00B5`) in `get-si-prefix-multiplier.ts` and `parse-and-convert-si-unit.ts` across amperes, farads, henrys, seconds, and meters.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `basic.test.ts` verifying both `parseSiUnit("1μ")` and `parseAndConvertSiUnit("10μH")` cleanly convert to $10^{-6}$ without precision loss or formatting defaults.

title: Accelerate large-board exact DRC repair
description: Removes the large-board skip for the bounded via-in-pad DRC repair phase, allowing exact repair candidates to be constructed with copy-on-write route cloning and sparse via materialization, while preserving existing DRC tolerances and safety budgets.
body:
## Summary

- remove the large-board skip for the bounded via-in-pad DRC repair phase
- construct exact repair candidates with copy-on-write route cloning and sparse via materialization
- group simplified traces in one pass and keep exact trace-pair segment searches route-local
- preserve the existing finite iteration, per-step candidate, and detour-variant budgets

## Why

Exact repairs mutate one route at a time, but candidate setup was repeatedly cloning, materializing, and scanning the entire board. That cost led us to skip the via-in-pad repair phase on boards with more than 120 routes and more than 3 via-in-pad issues. This makes the exact candidate path proportional to the affected route for those setup operations so the bounded phase can run on large boards.

This does not weaken DRC tolerances and does not remove safety budgets. Full candidate DRC evaluation remains unchanged.

## Validation

title: Route SRJ buses with path attraction
description: Summary consume explicit SimpleRouteJson.buses physically order bus lanes from the more tightly clustered endpoint route each bus center-out attract each subsequent member to an already-routed adjacent path expose bus attraction radius and bonus options add an SRJ scheduling test and a dense BGA visual fixture  Why The Rust router already contains direction-aware path attraction, but the WASMSRJ orchestration never supplied bus membership or guide paths. As a result, tscircuit buses were routed as unrelated sequential nets. ## Summary

- consume explicit `SimpleRouteJson.buses`
- physically order bus lanes from the more tightly clustered endpoint
- route each bus center-out
- attract each subsequent member to an already-routed adjacent path
- expose bus attraction radius and bonus options
- add an SRJ scheduling test and a dense BGA visual fixture

## Why

The Rust router already contains direction-aware path attraction, but the WASM/SRJ orchestration never supplied bus membership or guide paths. As a result, tscircuit buses were routed as unrelated sequential nets.

## BGA prototype

The visual fixture uses a 10×10 BGA at 0.8 mm pitch and routes four 6-bit buses from inner pads to four board-edge headers on four layers.

Five-run comparison after warm-up:

| Metric | Baseline | Bus-aware |
|---|---:|---:|
| Routed traces | 24/24 | 24/24 |
| Autorouting errors | 0 | 0 |
| Vias | 48 | 48 |
| Bends | 54 | 48 |
| Routed length | 345.934 mm | 346.880 mm |
| Median solve time | 1136.2 ms | 1159.5 ms |

The bus-aware result uses 11.1% fewer bends with the same via count, 0.27% more copper, and about 2% more median runtime.

## Dependencies

- depends on tscircuit/core#2883
- authoring API is introduced by tscircuit/props#758

The krt-wasm tests supply `buses` directly at the SRJ boundary so this PR can validate the consumer before the upstream releases land.

## Summary

- update the board to `tscircuit@0.0.2153` / `@tscircuit/core@0.0.1521`
- update `@tscircuit/common` to `0.0.46` and carry the RP2040 schematic patch from [common #80](https://github.com/tscircuit/common/pull/80)
- let `<Microcontroller_RP2040 />` own its four internal schematic sections
- split the schematic into `RP2040 Controller`, `Dual Motor Driver`, and `USB-C PD Motor Power` sheets
- use the built-in section layout for local decoupling and support components
- refresh the complete three-sheet schematic snapshot
- update the power-trace solver from [power-trace-expander #5](https://github.com/tscircuit/power-trace-expander/pull/5)
- retain top and bottom solder-mask-covered GND copper pours

## Schematic layout

The board now only assigns the RP2040 subcircuit to the `controller` sheet. The four controller sections are declared by `@tscircuit/common`, inherit that sheet through the released core behavior, and use instance-scoped internal names.

The section packer places local flash, USB, clock, motor-driver, and PD decoupling components near the parts they serve. The six identical RP2040 IOVDD capacitors now form one aligned parallel bank between a V3V3 rail and a GND rail, below the RP2040 and clear of its GPIO labels.

Regression coverage checks:

- all schematic component boxes on all three sheets stay inside their A4 inner frames with 0.5 mm clearance
- Circuit JSON contains no `schematic_element_outside_sheet_warning`
- the four common-owned RP2040 section titles belong to the controller sheet
- the IOVDD bank is exactly one aligned row of six with clearance from U1
- local decouplers remain within bounded distances of U1, U2, J_USB, Y1, DRIVER, and U_PD

`tsci check schematic-placement` emits `SchematicBoxPositions` only, with no errors or warnings.

The compatibility patch for [core #2780](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/2780) is removed because the fix is released in core `0.0.1520`. Temporary patches remain for:

- [CLI #3808](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/3808), rebased onto CLI `0.1.1748`, for sheet-aware placement checks
- [common #80](https://github.com/tscircuit/common/pull/80), against common `0.0.46`, until the common-owned RP2040 sections are published

Both patches apply cleanly to pristine npm tarballs.

## Power routing and DRC

The reroute phase relocates routed vias out of connected pads, including connectionless child traces, and retains clearance, simplification, shoving, layer-change, and redundant-via-pair cleanup.

The upper `P_MOTOR_A` trace receives a targeted first pass so it keeps the wide bottom-layer corridor. On the current router geometry it has:

- two routed vias
- 7.06 mm of bottom-layer copper
- 94.77% conservative nominal-width coverage
- 0.986 mm average width
- one unavoidable 0.903 mm continuous neck at the DRV8833 package exit

The complete board has:

- zero circuit errors
- zero `@tscircuit/checks` routing issues
- zero routed-via/SMT-pad overlaps
- zero vias on the `R_ISEN_B` trace
- no power pad-clearance result below the 0.1 mm hard DRC rule
- at most 14 preferred 0.15 mm clearance misses, confined to dense package escapes

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx tsci check schematic-placement index.circuit.tsx` — no issues or warnings
- `bun test tests/schematic-sheets.test.tsx` — 16 assertions passed
- `bun test tests/board.test.tsx` — 33 routing/DRC assertions passed in 129.8 s
- broad three-sheet schematic snapshot refreshed and visually inspected

title: Repair post-expansion trace clearance
description: Adds a granular, visualizable final clearance-repair solver phase that validates trace segments and relocates vias out of connected pads, ensuring compliance with clearance requirements and improving trace routing integrity.
body:
## Summary

- add a granular, visualizable final clearance-repair solver phase
- validate every trace segment with direction-independent endpoint-width semantics
- relocate routed vias out of connected pads, including fine-pitch grid-aligned escape lanes
- transactionally shove blocking traces, including locally routed child traces that are absent from the parent connection list
- expose repair and unresolved metrics through solver stats and add a debugger fixture for the connectionless-trace case

## Why

`@tscircuit/core` can reverse a solver route when it maps the result back to a source trace. A transition that was validated using the first endpoint width could therefore be serialized using the larger second endpoint width and produce a trace-to-trace DRC violation. The upgraded RP2040 motor-controller route also exposed three vias placed in connected pads. Two of those vias were trapped behind dense RP2040 fan-out copper, including an internal subcircuit trace that the parent routing problem did not list as a connection.

The final clearance phase now checks transition widths conservatively. The cleanup phase separately detects routed vias inside connected pads, evaluates radial plus 0.1 mm grid-aligned escape lanes, and uses the existing granular local-inflation solver to shove blockers transactionally. If the shove and relocated route do not revalidate, all trace changes are rolled back.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 35 passed, 418 assertions
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `git diff --check`
- RP2040 dual-motor benchmark passes in 13.3 s, below the 20 s guard
- captured current-router RP2040 output: 3 vias relocated, 0 unresolved, and 0 remaining via/pad overlaps
- current-router transition repair retains zero remaining or unresolved trace-clearance collisions
