title: Support selectable mapped ports on schematic symbols
description: Models schematic-symbol library pins as real, selectable Port children, initializing those ports through the established InitializePortsFromChildren lifecycle, mapping symbol ports to physical chip ports through explicit chipRef and connections, and reusing the mapped physical ports source and PCB identity for schematic and PCB traces.
body:
## Summary

- model schematic-symbol library pins as real, selectable `Port` children
- initialize those ports through the established `InitializePortsFromChildren` lifecycle
- map symbol ports to physical chip ports through explicit `chipRef` and `connections`
- reuse the mapped physical port's source and PCB identity, so schematic traces and PCB traces describe the same electrical connection
- forward `displayName` through the schematic symbol's source component

## Selector behavior

A mapped schematic symbol is a sibling of the physical chip; `chipRef` establishes an electrical mapping, not component containment.

```tsx
<chip name="Q1" ... />

<schematicsymbol
  name="Q1A"
  chipRef=".Q1"
  symbolName="n_channel_e_mosfet_transistor_horz"
  connections={{
    gate: "Q1.G1",
    source: "Q1.S1",
    drain: "Q1.D1",
  }}
/>
```

Therefore:

- physical chip selectors remain valid, such as `Q1.pin1` and `Q1.G1`
- schematic-symbol selectors are rooted at its own name, such as `Q1A.pin3` and `Q1A.gate`
- selectors such as `.Q1 > .A` are not introduced because the schematic symbol is not contained by `Q1`

Pin numbers on the library symbol do not have to match physical package pin numbers. In the MOSFET test, `Q1A.pin1` (drain) maps to `Q1.pin7`, while `Q1A.pin3` (gate) maps to `Q1.pin1`, according to `connections`.

Both `chipRef` and `connections` are required for mapping. Supplying only one emits a `source_property_ignored_warning`. Port labels are not auto-matched.

The referenced chip remains the only physical PCB component. A trace may target either the schematic-symbol port or the mapped physical chip port and will use the same underlying electrical and PCB port identity.

## Testing

- `bun test tests/components/primitive-components/schematic-symbol-*.test.tsx`
- `bun run build`
- schematic and PCB snapshot coverage in the mapped MOSFET tests
- explicit assertions that `Q1A.pin1` maps to `Q1.pin7` and `Q1A.pin3` maps to `Q1.pin1`

title: Auto-place coordinate-less explicit netlabels
description: Fixes the placement of coordinate-less explicit netlabels by routing them through the schematic trace solver, ensuring proper ownership and avoiding collisions with existing labels.
body: ## Fix ## What changed - route every explicit `` without `schX` / `schY` through the schematic trace solver - keep labels with explicit schematic coordinates on the direct/manual placement path - keep placement metadata separate from Circuit JSON records; no runtime component is attached to `SchematicNetLabel` - update the existing user-defined label with the solver-selected anchor instead of inserting a duplicate - keep the coordinate ownership checks inline at each pipeline boundary instead of introducing a helper module for the two-property predicate - update repro160 so U1's GND rail routes outward and down like the U1A representation - update affected snapshots for intentional solver placement of coordinate-less netlabels ## Root cause A coordinate-less explicit netlabel was initially anchored directly on its connected port and then classified as a pre-existing label. That prevented the collision-aware schematic trace solver from owning its placement. In repro160 this placed GND on the nested U1 representation and either required a distant manual coordinate or overlapped adjacent pins when the coordinates were removed. ## Placement ownership - `schX` or `schY` supplied: the user owns placement and the existing direct-render path is used - neither supplied: the schematic trace solver owns placement, regardless of how many schematic representations the source port has ## Validation - repro160 snapshot - updated RP2040, repro61, and opamp simulation schematic snapshots, visually verified - the opamp transient graph is unchanged; only its embedded schematic layout changed - six adjacent netlabel / schematicbox regression tests - `bunx tsc --noEmit` - Biome formatting and `git diff --check`

title: Connect thermal vias contained by footprint pads
description: Fixes connectivity issues for thermal vias contained within footprint pads by ensuring they inherit connectivity from the pads they are contained in.
body:
## Summary

Fixes the remaining `tsci check shorts` failures in `tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller` by assigning unconnected footprint vias to the connected pad that fully contains them.

## Root cause

A `<via>` only received connectivity metadata when it had an explicit `connectsTo`. The four DRV8833 thermal vias are unannotated footprint primitives placed entirely inside the pin 17 exposed GND pad, so core emitted them without a `pcb_trace_id` or `subcircuit_connectivity_map_key`. Downstream short detection therefore treated each intended pad/via contact as a collision between different nets.

## Fix

- Detect an unassigned via fully contained by a pad in the same footprint.
- Inherit connectivity only when the containing pads resolve to exactly one unique port.
- Link the emitted `pcb_via` to that port's source trace and copy its subcircuit connectivity key.
- Preserve explicit `connectsTo` behavior and leave standalone or ambiguous vias unassigned.
- Update merged repro162 to assert all four thermal vias resolve to the exposed pad's GND network.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repros/repro162-footprint-thermal-via-connectivity.test.tsx tests/repros/repro108-footprint-composite-pin.test.tsx tests/subcircuits/subcircuit-circuit-json-pcb-via.test.tsx tests/components/pcb/calc-pcb-position-via-board-relative.test.tsx`
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- Ran `@tscircuit/check-shorts` against the DRV8833 pad/via geometry: zero shorts

The full repository suite was also attempted; unrelated environment-dependent tests failed because local test servers could not bind port 0 and the model CDN was unavailable.

## Summary

Adds a focused regression reproduction for the remaining `tsci check shorts` failures in `tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller`.

The DRV8833 footprint contains four thermal vias inside its pin 17 exposed GND pad. Core correctly resolves the pad to `net.GND`, but emits each overlapping via without a `subcircuit_connectivity_map_key` or `pcb_trace_id`, so downstream connectivity/short checks treat the intended pad-to-via contact as a short.

This PR intentionally records the current behavior without implementing a fix. The test uses the DRV8833 exposed-pad and via dimensions/offsets, asserts that the pad resolves to GND while all four vias remain disconnected, and includes a PCB snapshot.

title: Prevent duplicate nested schematic net labels
description: Prevents duplicate fallback net labels for nested schematic boxes when the same source port has another schematic representation on the same sheet.
body:
## What changed

- detects child schematic ports whose port-to-net trace is owned by another subcircuit routing pass
- suppresses the child connection only when the same source port has another schematic representation on the same sheet, such as the parent `schematicbox`
- preserves child-side net labels when no alternate visual representation exists
- updates the `repro160` schematic snapshot to remove the duplicate GND rail while preserving the explicit U1 connection and the U1A GND representation

## Root cause

In repro160, U1 and U1A are two schematic representations of the same source component. The GND port-to-net source trace belongs to the parent board, but the child `workaround` pass also treated its U1 representation as needing a fallback GND label. Both passes therefore visualized the same logical connection.

Trace ownership alone is not enough to suppress a child label: ordinary cross-subcircuit connections still need endpoint labels inside each child. The fix combines stable source-trace ownership with Circuit JSON schematic-port identity. A child port is skipped only when an externally owned port-to-net trace can be rendered through another schematic representation of that exact source port on the same sheet.

The implementation performs a targeted Circuit JSON lookup by `source_port_id` only for externally owned port-to-net traces. This avoids root component-tree selection and keeps the decision local and deterministic.

## Impact

Nested schematic boxes no longer generate duplicate fallback net labels for parent-owned connections. Ordinary child subcircuits keep the endpoint labels needed to show their connections to parent nets.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/components/normal-components/chip-with-subcircuit-net-label.test.tsx tests/repros/repro160.test.tsx tests/repros/repro126-trace-overlap-box-resistor.test.tsx tests/repros/repro156-schematicbox-chipref-netlabel.test.tsx tests/repros/repro154-subcircuit-exposed-port-schematic-connections.test.tsx tests/repros/repro-boxed-subcircuit-internal-port-name-leak.test.tsx tests/repros/repro-boxed-subcircuit-missing-fallback-label.test.tsx tests/repros/repro-subcircuit-cross-boundary-trace-name-label.test.tsx tests/groups/group-schematic-box-connected.test.tsx`

title: Throw descriptive EasyEDA proxy authorization errors
description: Throws descriptive errors for EasyEDA proxy authorization failures by including specific error codes in the thrown error message when a 401 response is received, while preserving existing behavior for other responses and adding a focused test for session expiration.
body:
## What changed

- When the EasyEDA proxy returns HTTP 401, read its JSON error_code and include it in the thrown error.
- Remove the onProxyResponse callback and response metadata types.
- Preserve existing behavior for every non-401 response.

title: Preserve variable trace widths in copper-pour clearance
description: Fixes variable-width PCB traces being converted into a single copper-pour obstacle using only the first route width.
body:
## Summary

Fixes variable-width PCB traces being converted into a single copper-pour obstacle using only the first route width. This follows the merged reproduction in #65.

## Root cause

`convertCircuitJsonToInputProblem` grouped every consecutive wire point on a layer into one `InputTracePad`. `currentWidth` was initialized from the first point and never updated, so a route widening from 0.4 mm to 1 mm was cleared as 0.4 mm along its full length.

## Fix

When a wire point changes width, finish the current trace obstacle at that transition point and begin a new obstacle at the same point with the new width. Sharing the transition point keeps the clearance geometry continuous while preserving each segment width.

The minimal regression now verifies both widths and the shared transition point.

## Motor-controller impact

The top and bottom snapshots have been updated to reflect correct clearances around widened traces. Regenerating the complete `rp2040-motor-controller` pours with this branch and running `tsci check shorts` reduces findings from 28 to 4. The 24 trace/pour overlaps, including BOUT2, AISEN, and BISEN, are removed. The remaining four findings are GND-via contacts around the driver exposed pad and are outside this variable-width fix.

## Validation

- `bun test`: 35 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run build`: pass
- Biome check on changed TypeScript files: pass
- Complete motor-controller top and bottom SVG snapshots regenerated and visually inspected

body:
## What changed

Adds two complementary reproductions:

1. A minimal circuit-json test showing that a same-layer trace whose width increases from 0.4 mm to 1.0 mm is converted into solver input containing only the initial 0.4 mm width.
2. The complete `tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller` circuit as a solver fixture, with top- and bottom-layer SVG snapshots generated using its original GND pour settings (`0.2 mm` pad/trace margins and `0.3 mm` board-edge margin).

The full-board fixture excludes only previously generated `pcb_copper_pour` output elements so the solver recreates the pours under test.

## Why

`convertCircuitJsonToInputProblem` currently groups all consecutive wire points on a layer into one `InputTracePad` and assigns the first route point's width to the entire group. The wider portion is therefore passed to the copper-pour solver as 0.4 mm, which can leave copper inside the required clearance and create shorts.

This was reduced from the shorts reported by `tsci check shorts` in `tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller`.

## Observed behavior

The input route contains widths `[0.4, 1, 1]`, while the generated trace-pad widths are `[0.4]`. The test records that current behavior and explains that the 1 mm section is lost.

## Validation

- Both complete motor-controller layer snapshots pass deterministically.
- Biome formatting/check passes for the added tests.
- `bun test`: 35 pass, 0 fail.

This is a test-only draft PR; it does not include the fix.

title: Load serialized region assignments as initial routing state
description: Load existing region assignments from SerializedHyperGraph into the numeric routing state, allowing for normal rip-and-reroute behavior while keeping preloaded routes out of the initial pending queue.
body:
## Summary

- load existing `regions[].assignments` from `SerializedHyperGraph` into tiny-hypergraph's numeric routing state
- seed route-owned port assignments, region segments, intersection caches, and congestion cost without adding regions or ports
- keep preloaded routes out of the initial pending queue while allowing normal rip-and-reroute behavior when congestion requires it
- serialize solved route segments back into standard region assignments
- render preloaded assignments on their actual layer at iteration zero

## Why

`SerializedGraphRegion.assignments` already describes which connection occupies the chord between two existing region ports. A separate graph-level fixed-occupancy schema duplicated that model and incorrectly made preloaded traces permanently immutable.

This implementation uses assignments as ordinary solver state. Intersections between preloaded and newly routed traces are therefore included in the same region intersection cache and cost calculation.

No change to `@tscircuit/hypergraph`'s serialized schema is required.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- 96 non-image tests pass, including assignment loading, reripping, crossing detection, output round-tripping, bus-routing compatibility, and iteration-zero layer rendering
- `bun run build`

Three local image-snapshot test files cannot load the checkout's missing macOS `sharp` native binary; GitHub Actions runs the complete suite.

title: Handle connected copper in fanout clearance
description: Fixes clearance validation to treat connected copper as electrically connected rather than a foreign obstacle, improving routing success in fanout scenarios.
body:
## Summary

- add the exact serialized clad1 RP2040 fanout input as `dataset06`
- fix clearance validation so copper whose `connectedTo` list contains the connection name is not treated as a foreign obstacle
- add a focused regression for crossing same-connection copper
- render failed datasets as visibly labeled best-attempt snapshots and check in the clad1 image

## Verified improvement

The exact fixture contains:

- 132 top-layer connections and 132 atomic buses
- 265 mixed-footprint obstacles
- one shared component-area boundary
- `escapeLayers: ["top"]`
- `compactBusTracks: true`
- `borderDistribution: "even"`
- no alternate escape layer

Same-connection copper awareness improves the deterministic best attempt from 35/132 to 37/132 connections.

![clad1 RP2040 fanout snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/agent/add-clad1-rp2040-repro/docs/images/dataset06/sample001.png)

The snapshot is intentionally labeled `INCOMPLETE 37/132`; this PR does not claim a complete route.

## Remaining fanout features surfaced by the repro

1. **Non-monotone single-layer escapes.** At least one left-targeted connection has the RP2040 pad field and exposed pad directly to its left. A valid escape must initially move away from the requested boundary, route around the copper, and then turn back. The current lane and push/shove solvers are monotone.
2. **Mergeable multi-terminal electrical nets.** Repeated `source_net_*::fanout:*` terminals are currently allocated as mutually exclusive traces even when they share one `netConnectionName`. Routing them as one mergeable tree would remove artificial same-net congestion.

As a cross-check, the capacity autorouter's tiny-hypergraph pipeline reduced the full case to two unresolved high-density nodes at effort 2, but did not produce a complete accepted route after about 4.5 million iterations. That result is not committed or counted as success.

Refs #4.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 22 passing
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- visual inspection of `docs/images/dataset06/sample001.png`
